Full-Time Employment Contract A

Agreement effective 1 September 2026

This agreement is between PeopleFlow Demonstration Services (the Employer) and [PERSON] (the Employee). Employment commences on 2026-09-01. The Employee is appointed to administrative service work in the Operations team, reporting to the assigned team manager.

1 Employee particulars

[PERSON]; [ADDRESS]; [EMAIL]. Annual base salary: USD 50,400.00, paid as USD 4,200.00 gross each month.

2 Hours and place of work

The contracted working time is 40 hours/week, normally Monday through Friday, eight scheduled hours each day. Unpaid breaks fall outside those hours. The workplace timezone configured in PeopleFlow governs attendance and roster boundaries. Any change to the normal roster requires manager confirmation and must preserve the weekly total unless separately approved overtime applies.

3 Salary and payment

The annual base salary is USD 50,400.00, payable in 12 equal gross monthly installments of USD 4,200.00, less applicable deductions. The Employee must arrange verification of the payment destination through HR Payroll. Payment details must not be changed by editing a support attachment.

Payroll cutoff is the 20th calendar day at 17:00 UTC. Payslips are published by 18:00 UTC on the last business day of the month. Settlement may take two business days after the stated pay date.

4 Leave and sickness

The Employee is entitled to 25 days per calendar year of annual leave and 10 days per calendar year of paid sick leave. Annual leave accrues in equal monthly portions; pending requests reserve the available balance. Only scheduled missed workdays consume either allowance.

Up to five unused annual leave days may carry over if approved by 15 December and must be used by 31 March. Sick leave does not carry over. The first three consecutive scheduled sick workdays may be self-certified; evidence is required from the fourth. The Annual Leave Policy and Sick Pay & Absence Policy govern administration.

5 Additional hours

Overtime requires prior manager approval. Eligible actual work above 40 hours in a week may be compensated in cash or TOIL at 1.5 times the contractual hourly base or 1.5 hours of TOIL per eligible hour. The weekly overtime ceiling is 8 hours; total work must not exceed 48 hours. The Overtime & TOIL Policy applies to calculation and use.

6 Probation and variations

A three-calendar-month probation period applies. It does not reduce the benefits in clause 4. Changes to hours, pay, contract type or entitlement require HR approval, an effective date and a new signed package. Neither a roster edit nor a profile change amends this agreement. Prior signed terms remain in the employment record.

7 Records and acceptance

Confidential records are handled under the Employee Data Privacy Policy. The Employee may dispute an administrative calculation within 10 calendar days of notification; HR targets a written response within five business days. Original attendance and signed terms must be retained during review.

Read the agreement and ask HR to correct any discrepancy before accepting it through My documents. Complete step-up MFA and retain the signature receipt with the signed copy.

Part-Time Employment Contract B

Agreement effective 1 September 2026

PeopleFlow Demonstration Services offers [PERSON] employment in the Operations team from 2026-09-01 on the following part-time terms. The role comprises administrative service work and reports to the assigned team manager.

Schedule of agreed terms

Item	Agreed term
Employee	[PERSON]
Contract	B
Working time	24 hours/week
Normal attendance	Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, eight scheduled hours each day
Annual salary	USD 28,800.00 gross
Monthly installment	USD 2,400.00 gross
Annual leave	15 days per calendar year
Paid sick leave	5 days per calendar year
Probation	Three calendar months

[PERSON]; [PHONE]; [EMPLOYEE_ID]. Annual base salary: USD 28,800.00, paid as USD 2,400.00 gross each month.

Working arrangements

Unpaid breaks are outside the contracted hours. The workplace timezone in PeopleFlow determines roster and attendance boundaries. A roster change requires manager confirmation and must preserve the weekly total unless overtime is separately approved.

The annual leave and sick-pay allowances in the schedule are the agreed part-time amounts. They must not be multiplied by another part-time factor. Probation does not reduce them.

Pay administration

Salary is payable in 12 equal gross monthly installments, less applicable deductions. Payroll cutoff is the 20th calendar day at 17:00 UTC. Payslips are published by 18:00 UTC on the last business day of the month; settlement may take two business days after the stated pay date. HR Payroll must verify the payment destination. A support ticket attachment cannot authorize a change of destination.

Taking leave and reporting sickness

Annual leave accrues monthly in equal portions. Pending requests reserve balance. Scheduled workdays alone consume annual or sick leave. Up to five unused annual leave days may carry into the next year with approval by 15 December; carried days expire on 31 March. Sick leave does not carry over.

The first three consecutive scheduled sick workdays are covered by self-certification. Medical evidence is required from the fourth. The Annual Leave Policy and Sick Pay & Absence Policy apply to requests, evidence and balances.

Work beyond the agreed hours

Prior manager approval is required for overtime. Eligible actual work beyond 24 hours in a week may receive cash at 1.5 times the contract hourly base or TOIL at 1.5 hours per eligible hour. No week may exceed 8 overtime hours or 48 total working hours. The Overtime & TOIL Policy governs awards and usage; the same work cannot earn both cash and TOIL.

Changes and acceptance

Any amendment requires HR approval, an effective date and a new signed package. A roster or profile edit cannot alter these terms. Previous signed agreements must remain in history.

Confidential records are restricted under the Employee Data Privacy Policy. Administrative calculations may be disputed within 10 calendar days of notification, with a written HR response targeted within five business days. The dispute does not permit prior attendance or signed terms to be overwritten.

[PERSON] should review the schedule and personal details before signing in My documents, complete step-up MFA and retain the receipt. HR must correct any discrepancy before acceptance.

Signed by [PERSON]: ____________________ Date: ____________________

Annual Leave Policy

Policy owner: HR Operations

Effective 1 September 2026

Entitlement and scope

Contract A grants 25 annual leave days, Contract B 15, and Contract C 28 per calendar year. Contract B's 15 days are already the agreed part-time entitlement and must not be multiplied by a second part-time factor. A day means the employee's scheduled workday; a half day means half of that day's scheduled hours.

Accrual and reservations

Entitlement accrues at one twelfth of the assigned annual amount at each month end. Keep the internal accrual ledger to four decimal places and round the displayed balance to two decimals. A midyear starter accrues only for complete calendar months of active employment under this policy. Pending requests reserve balance; approved requests consume balance. Rejected, withdrawn, and cancelled requests release their reservations or deductions. An employee may not submit a request that exceeds the available accrued balance.

Carry-over and scheduling

Up to five unused days may carry into the next calendar year if a manager approves carry-over by 15 December. Carry-over expires on 31 March of the next year and is consumed before current-year accrual. The rest expires at year end. Organization holidays and nonworking roster days do not consume annual leave. Submit requests at least five calendar days before the first absence; a manager may approve shorter notice with a recorded exception reason.

Approval and cancellation

Managers assess team coverage and should decide within two business days. They must record a reason when rejecting a request. From 2026-09-01, employees can cancel pending or approved annual leave themselves before its first scheduled shift starts. Cancellation restores the appropriate balance immediately and notifies the manager. Once the absence has begun, HR must review any correction. Annual Leave Request Guide and Leave Request Guide v2 describe the active interface. Leave Request Guide v1 is historical and its support-mediated cancellation process is superseded.

Policy decisions and reviews

HR Operations owns this policy and reviews it every 12 months. A scheduled review does not change an approved absence or a contractual entitlement. Amendments require an authorized approver, an effective date and a published replacement. The assigned contract controls numerical entitlement; team calendar settings cannot reduce it.

An employee may dispute an outcome within 10 calendar days of notification. HR records a linked case and targets a written response within five business days. The existing status and evidence remain in place while the review is pending.

Sick Pay & Absence Policy

Policy owner: HR Operations

Effective 1 September 2026

Eligibility

This policy sets out the contractual paid sickness allowances. Contract A provides 10 paid sick days, B provides 5, and C provides 12 each calendar year. Eligibility begins on the contractual start date, including during probation. Balances reset on 1 January and do not carry forward. Part-time Contract B already includes its agreed 5-day allowance; do not prorate it again.

Report and classify

Report sickness before the scheduled shift begins where reasonably possible using Sick Leave Reporting Guide. Charge only missed scheduled workdays. A nonworking weekend between sick workdays does not consume a day but does not restart the evidence threshold. A partial sick day can be charged as half a scheduled day when HR confirms the recorded work interval. Sick leave must not be converted into annual leave without a separately reviewed request.

Evidence and payment

Self-certification covers the first three consecutive scheduled workdays of an episode. Evidence is required from the fourth and should arrive within two business days of reaching that threshold. Until evidence is reviewed, the record remains Evidence pending. HR may provisionally withhold the disputed sick-pay portion but must preserve the reported absence. When evidence is accepted before cutoff, payroll includes the eligible amount; later acceptance produces a subsequent adjustment.

Confidentiality and exhausted balances

Medical attachments are restricted to HR absence administrators. Managers receive absence dates, return expectations, and whether evidence requirements are satisfied, not the clinical narrative. Once the paid balance is exhausted, remaining sickness is recorded as unpaid sickness pending HR review. Payroll must not silently borrow from next year's allowance. A correction creates an audit revision and recalculates the remaining balance. The case note below shows how a three-day self-certified absence affects the balance.

Balance calculation from a closed absence

Overtime & TOIL Policy

Policy owner: HR Operations

Effective 1 September 2026

Compensation basis

This policy governs payment and time off for approved additional work. Contract A and C have 40 contracted hours each week; B has 24. Eligible overtime is manager-approved actual work beyond the individual's contracted weekly hours, measured Monday through Sunday in the assigned workplace timezone. Absence hours, unused roster hours, and unworked planned overtime do not count as actual worked hours.

Approval limits

Submit planned overtime at least one business day before work starts. Managers approve the purpose, maximum eligible duration, and Cash or TOIL compensation choice. Duration uses 15-minute increments. The weekly overtime ceiling is 8 hours and the total-work ceiling is 48 hours. Both controls apply; permission for 8 overtime hours never authorizes exceeding 48 total hours. Shift arrangements must also preserve 11 consecutive hours of rest. Emergencies require a documented HR exception review, not deletion of actual attendance.

Calculation and rounding

Cash overtime pays 1.5 times the contract hourly base. Derive an hourly base from annual salary divided by 52 and then by contracted weekly hours; keep intermediate precision and round the final earnings line to two currency decimals. TOIL awards 1.5 hours per approved overtime hour and keeps balances in quarter-hour increments. Two eligible overtime hours generate three TOIL hours. The same work cannot produce both cash and TOIL.

Credits and adjustments

TOIL is capped at 40 hours and expires 90 calendar days after the overtime work date. Managers must split an award or change the compensation choice before approving a credit that would exceed the cap. Approved TOIL absence consumes the oldest unexpired credit first. Expiry does not automatically create a cash payment. Payroll cutoff is the 20th calendar day at 17:00 UTC. A later attendance correction requires a linked overtime recalculation, with the old award and any balancing entry retained in audit history.

Probation & Contract Changes

Policy owner: HR Operations

Effective 1 September 2026

Probation reviews

HR must keep the contract assignment and the signed terms aligned. A new contract normally includes a three-calendar-month probation period. HR sets the start date, review date, manager, and contract type before activation. Probation does not reduce the leave or sick-pay entitlement stated in the assigned contract. Managers should schedule a midpoint discussion after six weeks and a final review at least 10 calendar days before the probation end date.

Record the outcome

1. Open HR administration > Contracts and select the active assignment.
2. Record the review outcome and attach the reviewed decision document.
3. Obtain HR approval before changing probation dates or contract terms.
4. Notify the employee through My documents and retain the acknowledgement or signature receipt.

An extension is limited to one additional calendar month under this policy and requires a recorded reason before the original end date. If no decision is recorded, the system raises a review alert; it does not automatically dismiss the employee or create a signed extension. HR must resolve the record explicitly.

Amendments and effective dates

Changes to weekly hours, salary, contract type, or entitlement require a new effective-dated amendment. Never overwrite the old signed terms. The new assignment takes effect at 00:00 in the workplace timezone on the approved date. Salary changes starting midmonth use calendar-day proration: old monthly salary multiplied by old-term calendar days divided by month length, plus the equivalent new-term amount. Round only the final monthly base-pay line to two decimals.

Downstream controls

HR previews leave accrual, weekly overtime thresholds, and future roster compatibility before activating an amendment. Contract B entitlements are already part-time amounts and must not be prorated a second time. If the amendment is approved after the payroll cutoff on the 20th at 17:00 UTC, Payroll Operations records a separately identified adjustment in the next run. A rejected signature package leaves the existing contract active. Employee Documents & E-Signatures governs reissuing a corrected package and preserving the previous audit evidence.

Approval record

Before completing a change, check the effective dates, the approver's authority and the applicable contract version. Store the decision and reason in the restricted employee record. HR Operations reviews a sample of completed changes each month against the approval trail. Incorrect rule assignments are corrected prospectively; any retrospective adjustment is documented separately.

Policy changes require an authorized approver, an effective date and a published replacement. HR Operations reviews the policy annually. Administrative disputes should be raised within 10 calendar days of notification; HR targets a written response within five business days and retains the original evidence during review.

Employee Data Privacy Policy

Policy owner: HR Operations

Effective 1 September 2026

Who may access employee records

Employees can inspect their own profile, payslips, attendance, and signed packages. Managers can inspect team schedules, approval requests, and absence dates. HR absence administrators alone can inspect medical attachments. Payroll Operations can inspect payroll earnings and verified payment destinations. Each role must be limited to the fields needed for its assigned work.

Access approval and audit

Role requests require a business purpose and approval by the module owner. Access expires when a temporary assignment ends. HR reviews privileged roles quarterly on 15 January, 15 April, 15 July, and 15 October. The application records actor role, operation, record reference, timestamp in UTC, and decision outcome for sensitive changes. Audit logs must not contain passwords, reset links, MFA recovery secrets, or complete medical attachment text.

Retention schedule

Record class	Retention period	Trigger
Profile history	24 months	Employment ends
Payroll and signed contracts	7 years	Relevant calendar year ends
Medical attachments	12 months	Absence episode closes
Ordinary support attachments	90 days	Ticket closes
Access audit events	24 months	Event recorded

A documented investigation hold pauses deletion for the specific affected records only. The record owner reviews holds every 90 days. Backups expire on a rolling 35-day schedule; a deletion request does not rewrite every historical backup immediately. Restored data must be reconciled against the deletion ledger before normal access resumes.

Requests and incidents

An employee may request access or a correction through the secure Privacy request form. HR acknowledges within two business days and targets completion within 20 calendar days, subject to a documented investigation hold. Identity verification must precede disclosure. Wrong-recipient exports, exposed medical files, and unauthorized payroll views are security incidents under Support Escalation & Security Incidents. Do not attach the exposed information to another ordinary ticket. Preserve a restricted reference and ask the security response group to control further sharing.
Employee FAQ

Which annual leave balance applies?

Contract A grants 25 days, B 15 days, and C 28 days per calendar year. Your available balance reflects monthly accrual and existing reservations. Contract B's entitlement is already part-time. Up to five approved carry-over days can be used until 31 March.

Can I cancel approved leave?

Yes. In v2.0, open the request and choose Cancel leave before its first scheduled shift starts. This releases the balance immediately and notifies the manager. After leave starts, ask HR for review.

section_path: How do I fix a missing punch?
text:
How do I fix a missing punch?

Use My time > Attendance > Request correction within 14 calendar days while the payroll period is unlocked. Your manager must approve it. Recalculation runs within five minutes after approval. Locked or older records require HR Payroll review under Attendance Correction Guide v2.

section_path: Can I arrange a shift swap?
text:
Can I arrange a shift swap?

Employees initiate swaps in v2.0 at least 24 hours before the earlier shift begins. The colleague must accept within 12 hours, then the manager must approve. Until approval, follow the original roster. Both employees must meet the team, skill, rest and weekly-hour checks.

section_path: When can I see a payslip?
text:
When can I see a payslip?

Published statements appear by 18:00 UTC on the last business day of the month. PAY-404 means no published statement exists. A missing allowance may reflect the cutoff on the 20th at 17:00 UTC.

section_path: Who sees profile and sickness details?
text:
Who sees profile and sickness details?

Managers see business contact information and absence dates. Home address history belongs to authorized HR access, while medical attachments are restricted to HR absence administrators. Never put a medical attachment into an ordinary team message.
Manager FAQ

What should I approve first?

Start with the oldest pending request in Team > Approvals. Decide within two business days. Reminders arrive after one business day; HR escalation follows after three. Support ticket SLAs are separate.

Can I edit attendance directly?

In v2.0, decide the employee's correction request. Direct manager edits belong to v1.8. Locked records go to HR Payroll; do not remove a lock to clear the queue. Approved corrections recalculate within five minutes.

section_path: Does colleague acceptance finalize a swap?
text:
Does colleague acceptance finalize a swap?

No. Check both assignments for skills, weekly hours and 11 consecutive hours of rest, then approve or reject. Until approval updates both assignments together, the original roster applies.

section_path: Must I approve a leave cancellation?
text:
Must I approve a leave cancellation?

Employees cancel pending or approved annual leave before its first scheduled shift starts. You receive a notification; no further approval is needed. Started leave requires HR review. The former instruction to contact HR Support is historical.

Can a delegate approve everything?

A delegate acts only for the configured team and dates, without access to medical attachments or payslips. Self-approval is blocked and routed to an alternative approver. If APPROVAL-409 appears, reload: another decision has already been saved.

section_path: Does more attendance mean automatic overtime?
text:
Does more attendance mean automatic overtime?

No. Check prior approval and the actual-work interval. The 1.5 multiplier, 8-hour weekly overtime limit, 48-hour total-work limit and 40-hour TOIL cap still apply.

PeopleFlow Release Notes v1.8

Released 2026-03-01. These notes cover the version used through 2026-08-31. PeopleFlow Release Notes v2.0 describe the changes introduced on 2026-09-01.

Features available in v1.8

Employees could view their attendance timeline, submit annual leave requests, download published payslips, and upload employee documents. Managers could decide annual leave and overtime requests through the team dashboard. Session expiry was 30 minutes idle or 12 hours after login. Password lockout followed five failures in 15 minutes and lasted 30 minutes.

Attendance in this release

Employees could not submit attendance correction requests. They sent the original times, proposed times, and reason to their manager. Managers directly adjusted unlocked records within 30 calendar days; older or locked periods required HR Payroll. Attendance Correction Guide v1 contains that historical procedure.

Cancelling leave

Employees could submit leave themselves, but cancellation required contacting HR Support with the request reference and the requested action. HR recorded the cancellation and restored the balance. There was no employee Cancel leave control. Leave Request Guide v1 is the matching historical guide.

Shift swaps

Swaps were manager-initiated. Employees asked the manager to arrange a trade; the manager checked both workers' agreement, team skills, rest, and hour limits, then reassigned both shifts. There was no employee Propose swap button or colleague acceptance timer. The resulting schedule still required 11 consecutive hours of rest.

Upgrade boundary

The v2.0 cutover is 2026-09-01. New actions after cutover use current procedures even when they concern an earlier date, subject to payroll locks. Existing attendance events, leave balances, and published rosters are retained. PeopleFlow Release Notes v2.0 explains the new self-service requests, leave cancellation, and employee-initiated swap controls.

PeopleFlow Release Notes v2.0

Released 2026-09-01. This release replaces v1.8 and introduces employee attendance correction requests, leave cancellation, and shift swap proposals. The upgrade preserves historical records and audit events. Contract entitlements do not change because the application version changes.

New self-service actions

- Employees now submit correction requests from their own attendance timeline. The window is 14 calendar days and payroll must be unlocked. One pending request per workday is allowed. Managers approve or reject; approval recalculates within five minutes. HR Payroll handles locked or older periods, replacing the former direct manager-edit route.
- Employees now cancel pending or approved annual leave themselves before the first scheduled shift starts. Cancellation immediately releases the reserved or deducted balance and notifies the manager. Started leave still requires HR review. Employees no longer need to contact HR Support for every cancellation.
- Employees can propose a swap at least 24 hours before the earlier shift starts. The colleague must accept within 12 hours; the manager then approves. Until approval updates both assignments, the original roster applies. Team, skill, overlap, 11-hour rest and weekly-hour checks apply. Unaccepted proposals expire after 12 hours or at the earlier shift start, whichever comes first.

Fixes and limits

- The manager queue shows original and proposed attendance timelines side by side. Conflicting decisions return APPROVAL-409.
- Payroll export mapping failures consistently return PAY-EXPORT-017.
- TOIL and cash overtime rules are unchanged. Self-service does not unlock payroll, automatically pay extra attendance or expose medical attachments to managers.

For administrators upgrading from v1.8

Verify role mappings and delegation periods before using the new dashboard. Historical direct attendance adjustments remain visible as completed manager events. For an old date corrected after cutover, use Attendance Correction Guide v2 and the current HR exception route.
Leave Request Guide v1

Historical scope and entitlement

This edition applied from 2026-03-01 through 2026-08-31. From 2026-09-01 use Leave Request Guide v2, including for new actions on existing requests. Annual entitlements in this edition were A: 25 days, B: 15 days, and C: 28 days.

Submit leave in v1.8

1. Open My time > Leave and choose Annual leave.
2. Enter the first and last absence dates and review the scheduled workdays.
3. Select full days or half days, check the available accrued balance, and add a handover note.
4. Submit at least five calendar days before the first absence unless the manager records a shorter-notice exception.

Pending requests reserved balance. The manager could Approve or Reject and should respond within two business days. Approved requests consumed balance, while rejection released the reservation. Nonworking roster days and organization holidays were excluded. An overlap returned LEAVE-409. An invalid date range or unsupported fraction returned LEAVE-422.

Historical cancellation procedure

Employees had no self-service cancellation control. To cancel a pending or approved request, the employee contacted HR Support with the request reference, absence dates, and whether the entire request should be cancelled. HR checked whether leave had already started, reviewed any payroll impact, and recorded the cancellation. The employee then reopened the request to confirm Cancelled and checked the released balance. Sending the support message alone did not restore any days.

Historical exceptions and evidence

For started leave, HR reviewed actual attendance and any payroll export before deciding whether a retrospective correction was appropriate. Employees could not erase the original approved request. HR retained the support case reference with the cancellation event. If the original request was rejected rather than cancelled, the history remained Rejected and should not be relabeled to simplify a report. New actions from 2026-09-01 use Leave Request Guide v2, including self-service cancellation of unstarted leave, even when an old request was created under v1.8.
Leave Request Guide v2

Current guide

This v2.0 guide is effective from 2026-09-01 and supersedes Leave Request Guide v1. Annual leave submission remains employee self-service; cancellation of unstarted leave is now also self-service. The contract entitlements remain 25 days for A, 15 for B, and 28 for C. The upgrade does not reset balances or add entitlement. Annual Leave Policy governs monthly accrual and approved carry-over.

Submit and track

1. Open My time > Leave > Annual leave and select the first and last dates.
2. Check scheduled workdays, excluded holidays, and any half-day selection.
3. Review the balance impact and add a handover note without sensitive health information.
4. Select Submit and retain the request reference.
5. Monitor Pending approval, Approved, or Rejected in My requests.

Submit at least five calendar days before the first absence unless the manager records an exception. Pending requests reserve days; approved requests consume them. Managers should decide within two business days. LEAVE-409 means an overlap exists. LEAVE-422 means a date range or fraction is invalid. A success banner does not replace checking the saved status.

Cancel before leave starts

Open the pending or approved request and choose Cancel leave. Review the complete cancellation, confirm it, and check the new Cancelled status. PeopleFlow immediately restores the reservation or deduction and notifies the manager. No new manager approval or HR Support ticket is required. Partial cancellation is not available: cancel the entire unstarted request and submit a replacement for the dates still needed. The replacement needs approval and may encounter changed availability.

Boundary and payroll handling

Self-service cancellation closes at the first included scheduled shift's start, measured in the employee's workplace timezone. If the selected start date is nonworking, use the first scheduled shift included in the absence. After that boundary, HR reviews any correction against attendance and payroll. LEAVE-423 identifies a started request that cannot be cancelled through self-service. Cancelling a future request does not recall an existing payroll export. HR Payroll must reconcile an affected exported period separately. The old instruction to contact HR Support for every cancellation belongs only to superseded Leave Request Guide v1.
Login & Password Reset Guide

Access prerequisites

PeopleFlow requires an active organization membership and a supported browser: the current or immediately previous major Chrome, Edge, or Firefox release. Open the organization login page from the approved workspace bookmark. Account activation links expire after 48 hours. A pending invitation does not create a usable account until activation is completed. Authentication is independent of leave entitlement and payroll permissions.

Sign in and MFA

1. Select your organization, enter your work login, and choose Continue.
2. Enter your password. Passwords require at least 14 characters and cannot match the previous five passwords.
3. Enter the six-digit code from the enrolled authenticator. A code rotates every 30 seconds; set the device clock to automatic if codes are rejected.
4. Confirm the workspace name on the landing page before opening HR records.

Five failed password attempts within 15 minutes cause a 30-minute lockout. Additional attempts during the lockout do not shorten it. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or 12 hours after sign-in, whichever comes first. Unsaved forms are not automatically submitted when a session expires.

Reset a password

Choose Forgot password and submit the registered work login. The confirmation screen deliberately looks the same for known and unknown accounts. Reset links expire after 20 minutes and can be used once. Requesting another link invalidates previous unused links. After saving a new password, sign in again; the reset invalidates existing sessions but does not remove MFA enrollment.

Recovery boundaries

Lost authenticator access requires identity verification by the HR administrator before enrollment is reset. Support cannot disclose a recovery code or accept an approval through an ordinary chat message. HTTP 401 means the session is unauthenticated; HTTP 403 means a valid session lacks permission. AUTH-423 identifies a temporary lockout, while AUTH-410 identifies an expired reset link. Follow Authentication Troubleshooting if authentication still fails after one fresh sign-in attempt.

Employee Profile Management

HR Operations | Revised 1 September 2026

Profile ownership

The Profile module stores contact details separately from employment terms. Employees can edit their preferred display name, personal contact number, and home address. Legal name, employee identifier, and assigned contract require HR review. Changing an address does not change payroll residency rules automatically. Payroll Operations must confirm any tax configuration change separately before the next payroll cutoff.

Update contact information

1. Open My profile > Personal information and select Edit.
2. Enter the new contact details and choose the date the address becomes effective.
3. Review the old and proposed values on the confirmation panel.
4. Select Submit change and reopen Change history to verify the recorded result.

Contact edits save immediately except legal-name and primary-login changes, which enter Pending HR review. Review normally completes within two business days. The primary work login cannot be replaced with a personal address through self-service. A verified recovery address can receive reset messages only after HR enables that feature for the organization.

Validation and privacy

An address requires street, city, country, and postal code where the selected country uses one. Phone input accepts a leading plus sign and 7 to 15 digits; spaces and hyphens are removed for validation. PROFILE-422 means a required value failed validation. PROFILE-409 means another edit was saved after the form opened; reload and compare values before resubmitting.

section_path: A change taking effect next month
text:
A change taking effect next month

When a move is scheduled for 2026-10-01, enter that effective date rather than replacing the historical address for September. Managers see the business contact view and cannot browse a home address through the team directory. HR can view the historical address chain for authorized administration. If an address appears in an unrelated screen, report the exposure under Support Escalation & Security Incidents and do not copy it into an ordinary support description.

section_path: Contact record awaiting an address change
text:
Contact record awaiting an address change

[PERSON]; [EMAIL]; [PHONE]; [ADDRESS].
Annual Leave Request Guide

Choose the correct balance

Use My time > Leave to request annual leave. The assigned contract determines the annual entitlement: A provides 25 days, B provides 15 days, and C provides 28 days. A displayed available balance subtracts approved future leave and pending reservations; it is not simply the annual entitlement. See Annual Leave Policy for accrual and carry-over rules.

Submit a request

1. Select Annual leave, then choose the first and last absence dates.
2. Review the workday preview. Nonworking roster days and organization holidays are excluded.
3. Choose a full day or a half day where the roster permits it, then check the calculated deduction.
4. Add a handover note without medical details and select Submit.

Requests should be submitted at least five calendar days before the first day off. A shorter notice period requires a manager exception reason. Annual leave can be requested in half-day increments. A pending request reserves the requested balance until it is approved, rejected, withdrawn, or cancelled. LEAVE-422 indicates an invalid range or unsupported fraction. LEAVE-409 indicates overlap with another active absence.

Status and cancellation

Draft has no approval effect. Pending waits for the assigned manager; Approved authorizes the absence; Rejected records a reason. From v2.0, employees may cancel their own pending or approved annual leave before its first scheduled shift begins. Open the request, choose Cancel leave, review the released days, and confirm. Cancellation is immediate, restores the reservation or deduction, and notifies the manager. A started absence requires HR review and cannot be cancelled through self-service.

Calendar timing

The first-shift boundary uses the employee's assigned workplace timezone. A leave request beginning on a nonworking day uses the first included scheduled shift. Cancelling a request does not change an already submitted payroll export; HR must reconcile any affected export separately. Leave Request Guide v2 is the current detailed cancellation guide. Leave Request Guide v1 describes the superseded support-mediated procedure and must not be used for current requests.
Sick Leave Reporting Guide

Report an absence promptly

Use My time > Absence > Report sickness before the scheduled shift starts whenever reasonably possible. If illness prevents portal access, notify the manager through the established absence channel and ask HR to record the report. A notification is not a requirement to disclose a diagnosis to a manager. The portal accepts an initial open-ended report; add an expected return date when it becomes known.

Record the period

1. Select the first missed scheduled workday and the expected final missed workday.
2. Choose Sickness as the absence type and indicate whether the report is new or an extension.
3. Upload evidence only in the confidential medical attachment field if required.
4. Submit, then check that the absence status reads Reported or Evidence pending.

The paid sick allowances are 10 days for Contract A, 5 for B, and 12 for C per calendar year. Nonworking roster days do not consume the balance. Paid sick days do not carry over. A report does not guarantee payment; HR checks eligibility and the available balance under Sick Pay & Absence Policy. Do not request annual leave merely because a sick balance is exhausted.

Evidence and notification

Self-certification covers up to three consecutive scheduled workdays in one sickness episode. Evidence is required from the fourth scheduled workday and should be uploaded within two business days of that threshold. Consecutive episodes separated only by nonworking days count as one episode. Managers receive the absence dates and coverage impact, while medical attachments remain restricted to HR absence administrators.

On return to work

Select Confirm return on the first day back and review the charged scheduled days. If the expected end date changed, update it before confirming. ABS-413 means an attachment exceeds 10 MB; ABS-415 means the file is not PDF, PNG, or JPEG. Replace an unreadable file rather than adding repeated copies. Keep the clinical note in the confidential attachment field; the absence timeline only needs the dates and evidence status.

Absence case note

[PERSON], employee [EMPLOYEE_ID], reported [MEDICAL_INFO]. [MEDICAL_INFO].
Clock-In / Clock-Out Manual

Register actual time

Clock-in and clock-out record actual attendance, not merely the published roster. Open My time > Clock and confirm the workplace timezone displayed above the controls. A shift may cross midnight; always inspect both the date and the time. PeopleFlow stores timestamps in UTC and presents them in the workplace timezone. A daylight-saving transition is calculated from elapsed UTC time, not by subtracting displayed local clock labels.

Daily procedure

1. Select Clock in when work begins. Confirm that an open attendance session appears.
2. Select Start break when an unpaid break begins, then End break on return.
3. Select Clock out when work ends and review the closed attendance interval.
4. Check the daily total after the next calculation cycle, which runs every five minutes.

One open attendance session is allowed per employee. CLOCK-409 means an open session already exists or a repeated clock-out was attempted. It does not mean the first event failed. Refresh the timeline before retrying. CLOCK-422 means event ordering is invalid, such as a break end preceding its start. PeopleFlow does not manufacture a missing clock-out from a roster end time.

Breaks and missing events

A 30-minute unpaid break is expected for shifts longer than six hours, but the system deducts recorded breaks only; it does not silently deduct an unrecorded break. A missing break generates a manager review flag. Worked time equals the closed interval minus recorded unpaid breaks. A 09:00-17:30 interval with a 30-minute unpaid break produces 8.00 hours.

Corrections and exceptions

For current records, use Attendance Correction Guide v2 to submit a self-service correction request. Employees propose corrected values; approval still belongs to the manager. A terminal outage should be documented with the approximate event times and a workplace explanation. Do not enter another clock-in to close an earlier session. If the total remains zero after five minutes despite a closed interval, use Attendance Troubleshooting and include the attendance calculation status in the ticket.
Attendance Correction Guide v1

Historical scope

This procedure applied from 2026-03-01 through 2026-08-31. For actions taken from 2026-09-01, use Attendance Correction Guide v2. Retain this edition with completed manager adjustments. In v1.8 employees could see attendance events but could not submit a correction request themselves.

Manager-mediated correction

1. The employee checked My time > Attendance and identified the affected workday.
2. The employee sent the manager the original event times, proposed times, and a factual reason through the internal attendance channel.
3. The manager opened Team > Attendance, selected the employee and date, and chose Adjust record.
4. The manager entered the replacement values, recorded the employee's reason, and saved the adjustment.
5. The employee reopened the timeline after the next five-minute calculation cycle to confirm the result.

There was no employee Submit correction button and no employee correction-request status page. An email or chat message to the manager did not itself change the attendance ledger. The manager was responsible for checking the roster and retaining the explanation in the adjustment note. Manager adjustment history stored both previous and replacement timestamps.

Historical limits

Managers could adjust unlocked records within 30 calendar days of the workday. Older records or a locked payroll period required HR Payroll intervention. The same event-order rule applied: clock-in precedes breaks and clock-out, and unpaid breaks must remain within the work interval. ATT-LOCK meant the period was locked; ATT-422 meant the proposed timeline was invalid. Saving a note alone did not clear either condition.

Reading old evidence

A historical adjustment marked Completed means the manager directly saved the replacement values; it does not prove an employee self-service request existed. When investigating an August record after the September upgrade, use the audit event's creation date to identify the original workflow. New corrections, including requests concerning an old date, now use Attendance Correction Guide v2 and may still require HR for the locked period. Do not recreate old manager messages as new approval requests merely to imitate the current interface.
Attendance Correction Guide v2

Current correction model

This v2.0 procedure takes effect on 2026-09-01 and supersedes Attendance Correction Guide v1. Employees can submit correction requests for their own attendance; managers approve or reject them. Submission does not change the ledger. Use a correction for a missing event, an incorrect timestamp, or an incorrectly recorded break. Ordinary clock events remain governed by Clock-In / Clock-Out Manual.

Submit a correction

1. Open My time > Attendance, select the workday, and choose Request correction.
2. Review the original timeline and enter the complete proposed timeline, including unpaid breaks.
3. Enter a reason of 20 to 500 characters explaining what happened.
4. Review the proposed worked hours and select Submit request.
5. Save the request reference and check the Pending approval status.

Self-service is available within 14 calendar days of the affected workday while the payroll period is unlocked. At most one pending correction is allowed per workday. ATT-409 identifies a competing pending request. Withdraw the existing request before proposing a different timeline. Employees may withdraw pending requests but cannot approve their own requests. Manager decisions should be made within two business days.

Decision and recalculation

Approval replaces the affected timeline and triggers recalculation within five minutes. Rejection leaves the existing ledger unchanged and requires a reason. An employee can open the decision history to compare the original and approved values. A proposed 09:00-17:30 day with a 30-minute unpaid break should produce 8.00 worked hours after approval. An approved request that still shows zero hours after five minutes should be escalated using Attendance Troubleshooting.

Outside the self-service window

ATT-LOCK means payroll has locked the period, even if the date falls within 14 days. ATT-422 means the proposed event sequence is invalid. Requests outside the window or in a locked period go to HR Payroll for a controlled adjustment; the employee must not alter a different workday as a workaround. A manager can review requests in Manager Approval Dashboard but cannot use the old Attendance Correction Guide v1 direct-edit procedure to bypass v2.0 controls. The original events, request, decision, and resulting ledger revision remain linked for audit.
Shift Schedule & Swap Guide

Read the published roster

Open My time > Schedule and choose Week or Month. Only Published shifts are binding; Draft shifts may still change. PeopleFlow displays start and end times in the workplace timezone. A shift ending after midnight shows its end date explicitly. Managers should publish the next week's roster by Thursday at 16:00 workplace time.

Propose an employee swap

From 2026-09-01, employees initiate swaps in v2.0. The earlier v1.8 manager-initiated workflow is described only in PeopleFlow Release Notes v1.8.

1. Select a published shift and choose Propose swap.
2. Choose an eligible colleague's published shift and review both resulting assignments.
3. Submit at least 24 hours before the earlier of the two shift starts.
4. Wait for the colleague to accept within 12 hours of the proposal.
5. After acceptance, wait for manager approval before following the changed roster.

Acceptance by the colleague is not final authorization. The original assignments remain in force until the manager approves. A proposal expires after 12 hours without acceptance or when the earlier shift begins, whichever happens first. A withdrawn or rejected proposal does not modify either roster entry. An employee can withdraw before a manager decision.

Eligibility controls

Both employees must belong to the same scheduling team, hold the required shift skill tags, and have no overlapping assignment. The resulting schedule must preserve 11 consecutive hours of rest between shifts and stay within each employee's contracted weekly hours unless separately approved overtime exists. SHIFT-422 identifies a failed eligibility rule; SHIFT-409 identifies a shift already involved in a pending swap. Resolve the active proposal rather than creating duplicates.

Manager completion

Managers use Manager Approval Dashboard to compare both sides of the swap and record a reason if they reject it. Approval updates both assignments atomically and notifies both participants. If only one side appears changed, refresh once and submit a support incident instead of manually trading another shift. The swap does not transfer leave approvals, overtime approvals, or payroll allowances. Those records require their own checks when the new assignment changes eligibility.

Payslip & Payroll Portal Guide

Payroll Operations | September 2026

Access payslips safely

Open Pay > Payslips and complete step-up MFA if requested. Employees see their own payslips; team managers do not receive payslip access merely through management permissions. Payslips are published on the last business day of each month by 18:00 UTC. A Draft payroll run is not visible in the employee portal. Payment initiation and bank settlement are separate events.

Read the statement

1. Select the payroll month and verify the statement status is Published.
2. Compare base pay, approved allowances, overtime, deductions, and the net amount.
3. Open the line-item explanation for any unfamiliar deduction code.
4. Download the PDF only to an approved private location and sign out on shared devices.

The payroll cutoff is the 20th calendar day at 17:00 UTC. Approvals received later normally appear in the following month's adjustment run. PAY-404 means no published statement exists for that period. PAY-403 means the session lacks access; never ask a colleague to download a statement on your behalf. PAY-EXPORT-017 means an export mapping failed and belongs with Payroll Operations rather than password support.

Gross pay and net pay

Gross pay is the sum of base pay and eligible earnings. Net pay equals gross pay minus the displayed deductions; reimbursement lines are shown separately if the organization enables them. A payment marked Submitted confirms that the export was sent, not that funds settled. Allow two business days after the stated pay date before reporting a settlement delay, unless the destination is visibly incorrect.

Raise a discrepancy

Use Pay > Report discrepancy and select the period and line item. Describe the expected rule and link an approval reference where available. Do not include a bank destination in a general ticket field. Payment-destination updates require HR verification and a separate payroll review before cutoff. Payroll Troubleshooting explains allowance mismatches and export retries. A corrected payslip is issued as a new revision; the original remains in the restricted audit history.

September statement extract

[PERSON], [EMPLOYEE_ID]; September gross USD 4,200.00, deductions USD 840.00, net USD 3,360.00. Bank: Northmere Savings; account: [BANK_ACCOUNT]; routing: [BANK_ROUTING].
Overtime & Time-Off-in-Lieu Guide

Separate permission from recorded time

An attendance total above contracted hours does not automatically create payable overtime or TOIL. Obtain manager approval before the extra work starts. Contract A and C use a 40-hour week; Contract B uses a 24-hour week. Approved extra hours beyond the individual's contracted weekly hours qualify under Overtime & TOIL Policy. The weekly window runs Monday 00:00 through Sunday 23:59 in the workplace timezone.

Request extra work

1. Open My time > Overtime and select the planned date and estimated duration.
2. Describe the business reason and choose Cash or TOIL as the requested compensation.
3. Submit at least one business day before the work begins.
4. After approval, clock actual time using Clock-In / Clock-Out Manual and link the closed attendance interval.
5. Review the finalized eligible duration before payroll cutoff.

Requests use 15-minute increments. Overtime is limited to 8 hours per week and total work must not exceed 48 hours in the same week. HR can decline an otherwise approved request if the final roster violates rest or total-hour controls. Unauthorized extra time remains visible as attendance but is flagged for review rather than silently deleted or automatically paid.

TOIL calculation and use

Approved overtime converts at 1.5 hours of TOIL per eligible hour. Two approved hours therefore create 3.00 hours of TOIL. The balance cap is 40 hours. A request that would exceed the cap must be split or changed to cash before approval. TOIL expires 90 calendar days after the overtime work date and cannot be carried forward by submitting a draft absence.

Reconciliation

To take TOIL, choose the TOIL absence type, enter hours in quarter-hour increments, and obtain manager approval. Approved usage deducts hours from the oldest unexpired credit first. Cash overtime uses 1.5 times the contract hourly base and rounds only the final currency line to two decimals. OT-422 identifies an invalid duration or limit; TOIL-410 identifies an expired credit. Corrections to the underlying attendance may require the overtime award to be recalculated, with the prior award retained in history.

Manager Approval Dashboard

Manager desk guide | September 2026

Establish decision authority

Open Team > Approvals and check the active team and delegation dates. The dashboard combines annual leave, attendance corrections, overtime, TOIL usage, and accepted shift swaps. A notification count is a shortcut to pending work, not an authorization to view other teams. Managers cannot approve their own requests; those route to the next authorized manager or HR if no alternative is configured.

Process the queue

1. Filter by request type and sort by submission time, oldest first.
2. Open the full record rather than deciding from the notification preview.
3. Compare the dates, balance impact, roster coverage, and any conflicting request.
4. Choose Approve or Reject. Rejection requires a reason of at least 20 characters.
5. Confirm that the decision appears in history and the pending count falls.

Target a decision within two business days. PeopleFlow sends a reminder after one business day and escalates an undecided request to HR after three business days. These are internal queue targets and do not replace the support response SLAs in Support Priority & SLA Policy. Bulk approval is available only for annual leave and requires opening the batch summary; attendance corrections and swaps require individual review.

Type-specific checks

For annual leave, review coverage and contract balance under Annual Leave Policy. Current employees may cancel before leave starts without a new manager decision; the dashboard shows Cancelled afterward. For attendance, review original and proposed timelines before applying Attendance Correction Guide v2. Approval triggers recalculation within five minutes. For swaps, confirm colleague acceptance and inspect both replacement assignments, skill tags, weekly hours, and 11-hour rest intervals under Shift Schedule & Swap Guide.

Concurrency and confidentiality

APPROVAL-409 means someone else acted on the request after it was opened. Reload the record and read the saved decision before taking another action. A delegated manager may act only while the delegation is active. Managers can see absence dates and the evidence-complete indicator but not confidential medical attachments. A payroll lock discovered during attendance approval blocks ledger changes and routes the matter to HR Payroll. Do not clear the lock or reclassify a request merely to remove it from the queue.

Handover to a delegate

Before going on leave, check that the delegate's team and active dates are correct. The delegate can act only during that period and does not gain access to medical attachments or payment destinations. If an action is missing, check the selected organization and role rather than using another person's session.
Employee Documents & E-Signatures

Document workspace

My documents separates employee uploads, assigned acknowledgements, and signature packages. Uploading a file does not mean HR has accepted it, and acknowledging a policy does not execute a contract amendment. Document status can be Uploaded, Under review, Accepted, Rejected, Awaiting signature, or Completed. A signature package must contain the approved terms before it is sent to the employee.

Upload and review

1. Choose the correct document category before selecting a local file.
2. Upload PDF, DOCX, PNG, or JPEG up to 10 MB; password-protected files are rejected.
3. Confirm that the preview shows the intended pages and no unrelated material.
4. Submit for review and inspect the status after the upload scan finishes.

DOC-413 indicates a size limit, DOC-415 an unsupported type, and DOC-422 a protected or unreadable file. Scanning normally finishes within two minutes. Do not rename an executable to bypass a type restriction. HR may reject an incomplete upload with a reason; submit a new revision rather than overwriting a previously accepted file.

Sign an assigned package

Open the package from My documents, read every page, and choose Continue to signature. Complete step-up MFA, confirm the displayed signer identity, and select Sign. The service records the package hash, timestamp in UTC, consent version, and signer display name. A completed receipt is available alongside the signed copy. Invitations expire after seven calendar days; HR must reissue an expired package rather than backdate a receipt.

If the package is wrong

If the signer identity or terms are wrong, stop before signing and choose Request correction. A signature cannot be removed through self-service; HR issues a replacement package and preserves the previous audit trail. Managers can see completion status for assigned team acknowledgements but cannot browse identity uploads. The receipt shows who signed, which package was signed, and when. Keep it with the completed package so HR can trace a later replacement.

Completed signature receipt

[PERSON]; [EMAIL]; signed document SIG-2026-1012 on 2026-09-08 at 10:15 UTC.

How to Submit a Support Ticket

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

document_title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

metadata.title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

section_path: How to Submit a Support Ticket
text:
Start in the right channel

Help > Submit ticket creates a PeopleFlow support record. Use a ticket for a reproducible application failure or an unexplained result after following the relevant manual. Leave approval, attendance approval, and payroll authorization remain separate business processes. Creating a ticket does not approve a request, stop a shift, or guarantee a payroll adjustment. An active data exposure should use the security incident route in Support Escalation & Security Incidents immediately.

document_title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

metadata.title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

section_path: How to Submit a Support Ticket
text:
Required information

1. Select a category: Authentication, Absence, Attendance, Shifts, Payroll, Profile, or Technical.
2. Enter a short subject describing the affected action and visible result.
3. Describe expected behavior, actual behavior, and numbered reproduction steps.
4. Add the event time with timezone, application version, browser version, and exact error code.
5. Select impact and submit. Keep the assigned ticket reference for follow-up.

Priority is assessed by support under Support Priority & SLA Policy. Select High impact for an organization-wide outage, a payroll run blocked before cutoff, or suspected exposure of restricted data. A single delayed approval usually belongs in Medium or Low depending on its impact. Repeatedly submitting the same problem creates competing records and does not accelerate the response target.

document_title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

metadata.title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

section_path: How to Submit a Support Ticket
text:
Attachments and safe handling

Up to three PDF, PNG, JPEG, or text attachments are allowed, each no larger than 5 MB. Remove unrelated screen content and use the secure attachment classification for confidential records. Never upload passwords, tokens, or authenticator recovery material. TICKET-413 identifies a size breach; TICKET-415 identifies an unsupported attachment. If submission fails, retain the error code and retry once after removing the failing attachment.

section_path: How to Submit a Support Ticket
Keep the conversation in one ticket
text:
Keep the conversation in one ticket

The ticket below reports that a closed attendance interval still shows zero after the five-minute calculation cycle. Useful additional evidence is the record reference and calculation status, rather than an entire payroll export. Replies should remain in the original ticket so the diagnosis and resolution form one history. Support can request missing information and pause the resolution investigation while awaiting it; first-response commitments remain as defined in Support Priority & SLA Policy.

document_title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

metadata.title: How to Submit a Support Ticket

section_path: How to Submit a Support Ticket
text:
Ticket HR-2026-3001

Requester: [EMAIL]; [PHONE]; [EMPLOYEE_ID]. Subject: attendance total remains zero after clock-out. Ticket HR-2026-3001 contains no password or session token.

Support Priority & SLA Policy

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

Service calendar

PeopleFlow's standard support hours are Monday through Friday, 09:00-17:00 UTC, excluding 1 January and 25 December. A business hour counts only inside that window. A business day contains eight support hours. Security incidents use the continuous reporting route in Support Escalation & Security Incidents. The targets below concern a human first response, not a guaranteed fix or approval.

Priority	Qualification	First response	Update target
High	Organization-wide outage, blocked payroll run before cutoff, suspected restricted-data exposure	1 business hour	Every 2 business hours
Medium	One user cannot complete core work; workable alternatives are limited	4 business hours	Each business day
Low	Guidance, cosmetic defect, nonblocking request	2 business days	Every 3 business days

Clock examples

A Medium ticket opened Friday at 16:00 UTC receives one business hour on Friday and reaches its four-hour first-response deadline Monday at 12:00 UTC, assuming neither day is an excluded holiday. A High ticket opened at 18:00 UTC starts its standard response clock at the next business opening. Security reporting is available continuously, but continuous reporting is not a promise of a one-hour out-of-hours human response.

Triage and escalation

Support verifies scope, affected function, start time, and any workaround before confirming priority. A requester's selection is provisional. Reclassification records a reason and does not erase the original submission time. If a first-response deadline is missed, the queue lead is notified immediately. If a High incident has no workaround after four business hours, the application owner receives a technical escalation. A security incident goes directly to the security response group regardless of elapsed support time.

Resolution boundaries

Support response targets do not override manager approval targets, payroll cutoff, or contract entitlements. A ticket may be Waiting for requester when required evidence is missing. That state pauses any agreed resolution estimate, but never resets the already measured first-response result. Close a resolved ticket after confirmation or after five business days without a response to the proposed resolution. Reopen within 10 calendar days for the same unresolved issue; otherwise create a linked new ticket.

Authentication Troubleshooting

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

Triage the visible failure

Record the failed action and whether it happened before or after MFA. Use the code to choose the next step.

Code	Meaning	First action
HTTP 401	No valid authenticated session	Follow Session recovery below
HTTP 403	Signed in, but permission is missing	Check organization and ask HR to review the role
AUTH-423	Temporary lockout	Wait for the lockout to end
AUTH-DISABLED	Account disabled by HR	Ask HR to review; a password reset will not reactivate it

Do not clear cookies repeatedly before recording the failure.

Session recovery

1. Save unsent text locally without copying confidential record contents.
2. Sign out, close other PeopleFlow tabs, and reopen the approved workspace bookmark.
3. Sign in once and verify the selected organization.
4. Repeat the action on a nonsensitive record if possible.

If a new session resolves HTTP 401, the earlier session likely expired. Sessions expire after 30 minutes idle or 12 hours from sign-in. A recurring 401 immediately after sign-in may indicate blocked first-party cookies or a stale organizational login route. Use a supported browser and permit the organization's required first-party session cookies. Do not disable browser security globally.

MFA and lockout

Authenticator codes contain six digits and rotate every 30 seconds. Set automatic device time and use the next newly generated code once. Five failed password attempts within 15 minutes trigger a 30-minute lockout. Wait for the lockout to end rather than creating a series of reset requests. A password reset link lasts 20 minutes and is invalidated when a newer link is requested. AUTH-410 means the reset link has expired or been replaced.

Escalation and disabled accounts

Lost MFA enrollment requires HR identity verification before an administrator resets it. An AUTH-DISABLED account must be reviewed by HR; support cannot infer employment status or reverse deactivation. For persistent failures, submit browser and application versions, the error code, event time with timezone, and whether a fresh session worked. Never submit a password, MFA code, reset link, session cookie, or recovery secret. Support Escalation & Security Incidents applies if an unexpected authentication event suggests unauthorized access rather than an ordinary login failure.

Attendance Troubleshooting

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

Zero hours after a shift

PeopleFlow calculates closed intervals every five minutes. An open session may show zero worked hours until clock-out closes the interval. Check the timeline rather than repeatedly pressing Clock out. A 09:00-17:30 interval with a 30-minute unpaid break should total 8.00 hours. Calculation uses UTC elapsed time, which can differ from local label subtraction during daylight-saving changes.

Diagnostic sequence

1. Check the workplace timezone and both dates for overnight shifts.
2. Confirm that clock-in, any break events, and clock-out appear in sequence.
3. Wait one complete five-minute calculation cycle after the latest accepted event.
4. Refresh once and inspect the calculation status.
5. If a closed valid interval remains zero, report its record reference and status to support.

Missing and duplicate events

CLOCK-409 indicates an open session already exists or an already closed interval received another clock-out. Inspect the saved timeline before retrying; a duplicate rejection does not imply the original event was lost. CLOCK-422 indicates invalid ordering. PeopleFlow never invents a missing clock-out from the published shift end. Use Attendance Correction Guide v2 to request the missing event with an accurate reason and a complete proposed timeline.

Correction controls

Since 2026-09-01, employees can submit their own attendance correction requests within 14 calendar days of the workday if payroll is unlocked. Approval remains with the manager and triggers recalculation within five minutes. ATT-409 means a pending correction already exists; withdraw it before submitting a replacement. ATT-LOCK routes to HR Payroll. A request outside the window also requires HR Payroll review. Attendance Correction Guide v1's direct manager-edit procedure is historical and must not be used to bypass these controls.

Investigation evidence

Provide the affected date, timezone, visible event sequence, latest calculation state, correction request status, and exact error code. Do not attach unrelated team attendance or a full payroll statement. If approval succeeded but recalculation failed, support investigates the linked calculation job while HR retains the approved request. Do not edit another workday to compensate, and do not approve an overtime award against a known incorrect total.

Payroll Troubleshooting

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

Identify the payroll stage

Check whether the problem concerns eligibility, calculation, publication, export, or settlement. A manager-approved allowance is not necessarily in the current run if approval arrived after cutoff. Payroll cutoff is the 20th calendar day at 17:00 UTC. Payslips are published on the last business day of the month by 18:00 UTC. Payment settlement may take two business days after the stated pay date.

Missing allowance procedure

1. Open the affected period in Pay > Payslips and check the revision number.
2. Compare the allowance approval timestamp with the cutoff.
3. Check the allowance's effective dates and whether the attendance condition was satisfied.
4. Submit Pay > Report discrepancy with the approval reference and disputed line.

An approval after cutoff normally appears in the following month's adjustment run. An approval before cutoff that is missing from a Published statement needs Payroll Operations review. Support should not add an allowance manually or change an approval timestamp to force inclusion. PAY-404 means no statement is published; PAY-403 means access is denied rather than a calculation failure.

Export failures

PAY-EXPORT-017 means a configured export mapping is missing or invalid. Payroll Operations checks the rejected field, fixes the mapping, validates the full batch, and retries using the same payroll run reference and a new export attempt number. Check the previous attempt's delivery status before retrying to prevent duplicate payments. An export marked Submitted is not proof of bank settlement. Never resolve an export failure by replacing a destination with a colleague's payment details.

Confirm the corrected statement

Compare the base pay, allowance and deduction lines in the statement below. Verify that gross minus deductions equals net before investigating settlement. A corrected published statement receives a new revision and preserves the prior copy. Close the discrepancy only after Payroll Operations records the approved resolution, the employee can see the correct revision, and any required export or next-run adjustment is linked.

Statement under review

[PERSON], [EMPLOYEE_ID]; September base USD 3,200.00 plus approved allowance USD 120.00; gross USD 3,320.00; deductions USD 664.00; net USD 2,656.00. Payment destination: [BANK_ACCOUNT] at Alderhaven Community Bank.

Support Escalation & Security Incidents

IT Support | Updated 1 September 2026

Choose an escalation route

Use Help > Escalations > Service queue for ordinary unresolved support work. Use Help > Security incident for suspected unauthorized access, wrong-recipient exports, exposed medical files, or unexpected payroll downloads. These are role-based application queues, not personal contact details. If normal sign-in is unavailable, use the Security report option on the organization's approved PeopleFlow login page. That form accepts reports continuously.

Immediate incident procedure

1. Stop the action that may be exposing information; do not repeat a bulk export to test it.
2. Record the first observed time with timezone, affected module, and a restricted record reference.
3. Report through the Security incident form and preserve the incident reference.
4. Follow containment instructions from the security response group.

Do not forward exposed records, copy them into public chat, delete audit evidence, or attempt to investigate another employee's account. If a shared link is involved, record its internal reference in the secure form rather than reposting the link. Security administrators may revoke sessions, disable the affected share, or temporarily restrict a role while preserving logs.

Ownership and timing

The service queue lead handles missed first-response targets from Support Priority & SLA Policy. A High service incident without a workaround after four business hours escalates to the application owner. Suspected security incidents bypass that waiting period and route immediately to the security response group. Continuous reporting does not create a separate guaranteed out-of-hours response SLA. The security response group assigns severity, directs containment, and decides who may receive an incident update.

Closure and communication

The incident owner records the affected scope, containment time, recovery checks, and remaining follow-up actions. HR Operations reviews any employee-facing explanation before it is distributed. Only authorized incident owners issue broad notifications. Closure requires confirmation that unauthorized access has stopped and the corrected permissions or configuration were checked. Retain relevant audit references under Employee Data Privacy Policy; an investigation hold pauses routine deletion for those records. An ordinary user should be told the safe next step without receiving unrelated confidential investigation details.
